content_metadata.description: A documentary-style video following the journey of Francis Kantavooro, a Biogas Engineer who innovatively converts plastic waste into usable fuel, showcasing both the technology and its socio-economic and environmental impacts.

qAndA.question: What type of container is used to collect the fuel produced by the reactor?
What is the color of the fuel produced by the reactor?

qAndA.answer: He believes the project will create jobs for collecting, sorting, and processing plastic waste, ultimately leading to income generation for families.
qAndA.question: Why does Francis believe his project can contribute to socio-economic growth?

qAndA.answer: He finds it very interesting, especially because it uses simple, readily available materials to create a valuable product.
qAndA.question: What is James Adomako's opinion on the project?

qAndA.answer: It serves as a powerful visual demonstration of the project's feasibility and effectiveness, reinforcing the hope and excitement surrounding its potential.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm motivation to work on this project came as a result of the plastic waste found on our
lands, especially the agricultural lands.
And I realized that if we don't take these plastic waste out of the environment, one
day it will be difficult to farm and living organisms within the micro-organism within
the soil will also be wiped out because of the release of hydrocarbons.
And also even the pollution of the ozone layer when these plastics are burned into the atmosphere.
Here are our raw materials.
You can see different kinds of raw materials, vaultic containers.
We have the sachet water, different kinds, different colors as you can see.
So here is our reactor, which is the third generation of the reactors that are built so far.
The first and the second generations were a little smaller than this one.
Now with this reactor you have the inlet.
This is the inlet where we feed the plastic waste through.
And within the reactor we have the feed unit, that is where the waste is located.
For the boiling process, melt in the boiling, and then the cracking chamber is at the top
of the reactor.
That is where actually the fuel is being formed.
And from there we create what we call the delivery pipe or the exits.
That is where the fuel passes out to the collection point.
So as you can see.
I began looking at the source of plastics waste.
And then it motivated me that I could be able to come out with petroleum components out
of the plastic waste.
And the most important thing is to take the plastic waste out of the environment,
otherwise even thought of probably making some money out of it.
But after I have been able to conclude certain findings and have tested my product, the diesel,
gasoline and the grease, I realized that one could even make money out of it well.
Helping other people to be engaged or be employed into the project.
It looks very interesting to me.
And being more or less a very local innovation.
Whatever I was using making it wasn't any complicated thing.
Very simple, drum, and some kind of maybe a local engineer trying to bring to life what
he's been thinking about with unsophisticated materials more or less.
So it's quite impressive to me.
If this project kicks off, we will feel that there will be a percentage of increment
in employment that will build a socio-economic growth of families.
We would have also felt that the plastics situation as we complain would have been of minimal
or no problem existence at all.
Because for example, if we build a 50 ton plant, it will mean that every day we will need
50 tons of plastic waste to go into the reactor for cracking.
Now I believe that we have such a plant.
That's just even a single plant.
The subsequent years people would have learned to send their plastic waste to a company like
that instead of throwing it anywhere.
It means that this plastic will no longer be found lying everywhere or litering around.
